diagnostics.support.overview-description: This preview summarizes the diagnostic data prepared for support. Sensitive names, paths, addresses, request metadata, and oversized collections are protected by the sanitized privacy profile before download.
This preview summarizes diagnostic data prepared in Full mode. Raw names, paths, addresses, URLs, and request metadata may be included, so review every section before downloading or sharing.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-saniti: Sanitized bundles are intended for safer support sharing. They preserve counts, health state, timing, relationships, and other troubleshooting structure while applying the treatments below to sensitive names, identifiers, paths, addresses, URLs, request metadata, and verbose collections before download.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-full: Full exports retain raw diagnostic values and may include container or VM names, filesystem paths, network addresses, URLs, request metadata, and other identifying details. Use full mode only when support specifically requests it, review the bundle before sending it, and share it through a trusted private channel.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-hashed: Replaces the original value with a short, one-way identifier derived using the export's private salt and field context. Repeated identical values in the same field path remain comparable within that bundle, helping support follow relationships without seeing the source value. The original value is not stored in or directly recoverable from the hash, and a later export produces different identifiers.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-masked: Obscures the sensitive portion while retaining only limited structure that can help diagnose a problem. Depending on the field, this may preserve a filename, URL path, value shape, or the first network prefix while hiding the identifying portion. Masked output is intentionally incomplete and should not be treated as the original value.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-omitte: Removes the raw field when it is unnecessary for diagnosis, usually replacing it with null, a safe structural summary, or a separate hash where correlation is useful. The redaction manifest records the affected field path, so support can distinguish deliberate removal from a collector failure. The removed value is not stored in the manifest.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-trunca: Bounds oversized strings, arrays, histories, logs, or deeply nested details so the bundle remains practical and avoids exporting excessive data. The retained portion still provides a useful troubleshooting sample, while the redaction manifest records that more content existed. Truncation describes a size limit, not a sanitization failure.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-salt: Hash scope: $1. Each sanitized export creates a fresh random salt and includes only a short fingerprint, not the salt itself. Hashes are therefore useful for correlation inside that bundle but intentionally change across later exports, preventing stable cross-bundle tracking.
diagnostics.support.data-handling-full-s: Hash scope: none for privacy redaction in full mode. Raw values are retained, although existing diagnostic limits may still bound long logs, histories, arrays, or deeply nested details. Review the bundle carefully because full mode is not intended for public issue reports.
